tagline: Costa Rica's most-visited national park squeezes rainforest trails, white-sand beaches and more wildlife per acre than almost anywhere — sloths and monkeys included.
overview: Manuel Antonio National Park is the smallest national park in Costa Rica and by far its most famous. Created in 1972 when locals pushed to protect the forest from development, it wraps jungle-covered headlands around some of the country's most beautiful white-sand beaches.

The park's trails are short but packed with life. Two-toed and three-toed sloths hang in the canopy, capuchin monkeys patrol the beaches, and the endangered Central American squirrel monkey — found almost nowhere else — leaps through the trees in troops. Iguanas, coatis and basilisk lizards are close behind.

The town hugs the jungle-lined road down from Quepos, the fishing port that calls itself the sailfish capital of the world. Offshore, catamaran tours snorkel quiet coves, and the mangroves of the Damas Island estuary offer calm boat trips through tunnels of roots where monkeys and crocodiles live.

funFacts.title: SMALL BUT MIGHTY
funFacts.text: Manuel Antonio is Costa Rica's smallest national park — and its most visited.

funFacts.title: A MONKEY FOUND ALMOST NOWHERE ELSE
funFacts.text: The grey-crowned Central American squirrel monkey survives mainly in and around this park.

funFacts.title: CLOSED FOR THE ANIMALS
funFacts.text: The park closes one day each week so the wildlife can rest from visitors.

funFacts.title: A BEACH VOTED WORLD-CLASS
funFacts.text: Playa Manuel Antonio regularly ranks among the best beaches in the world in traveller polls.

funFacts.title: OVER 100 MAMMAL SPECIES
funFacts.text: The park packs more than 100 mammal and 180 bird species into just a few square kilometres.

funFacts.title: AN ISLAND THAT JOINED THE COAST
funFacts.text: Punta Catedral, the park's landmark rock, was an island until sand built a natural bridge to it.

funFacts.title: THE SAILFISH CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Neighbouring Quepos hosts international tournaments and some of the best Pacific sportfishing.

funFacts.title: RAIDERS OF THE BEACH
funFacts.text: Capuchin monkeys on the beach are expert snack thieves — park rules ban feeding them.

funFacts.title: JESUS CHRIST LIZARD
funFacts.text: Basilisk lizards here can sprint across the surface of water on their hind legs.

funFacts.title: NAMED AFTER A SETTLER
funFacts.text: The park is named for a Spanish-era settler buried on Punta Catedral, marked by a wooden cross.
